1 JSON backend setup JSON files, helper functions, backend parity, and setup sequence.

Same frontend, different storage layer

The screen the user sees should stay familiar while the persistence layer changes from SQL to JSON. That is what makes the comparison between tracks honest.

By the end of this page, you should know exactly which parts of the app stay the same and which parts need new backend thinking.

What stays the same and what changes

AreaStill the sameNow different
templates/index.htmlThe user-facing layout can stay aligned with SQLThe page should not reveal storage details
static/js/app.jsThe browser still uses fetch and redraw logicThe routes now read and write JSON-backed data
app.pyFlask still handles the routesThe storage logic uses load/save helpers instead of SQL queries
data/*.jsonNew for HLThese files now hold the stored records

Where the JSON backend sits

The browser still talks to Flask. Flask now reads and saves document data instead of sending SQL queries.

Generic JSON track structure

project/
  app.py
  data/
    users.json
    tasks.json
  templates/
    index.html
  static/
    js/
      app.js
data/

This folder makes the storage-model change visible instead of hiding it in UI files.

templates/ and static/js/

These can stay conceptually aligned with the SQL version.

Python / JSON helper words

CodeWhat it doesWhy it matters
os.path.exists()Checks whether a file is already present.Useful when the task file may start empty.
load_tasks()A helper that returns the current stored records.Routes stay cleaner when repeated file logic is extracted.
save_tasks(...)Writes the updated list back to disk.A create, delete, or update action eventually needs this.
jsonify()Returns JSON back to the browser.The frontend contract stays familiar even when storage changes.

Generic load / save helper pattern

import json
import os

DATA_FILE = "data/records.json"

def load_records():
  if not os.path.exists(DATA_FILE):
    return []

  with open(DATA_FILE) as file:
    return json.load(file)

def save_records(records):
  with open(DATA_FILE, "w") as file:
    json.dump(records, file, indent=2)
os.path.exists

Protects the app from crashing when a file is not there yet.

return []

An empty list is a sensible starting state for many JSON-backed record sets.

json.dump

Writes the whole updated structure back to disk.

Validation still matters in HL

HTML

The browser can still guide the user with required fields and sensible controls.

JavaScript

The browser can still package and check values before sending them.

Flask

The backend must still reject weak or inconsistent values.

JSON write step

The final saved structure still needs consistent keys and reliable ids.

Work through the HL setup in this order

This is the preparation run before the first JSON feature page.

Step 1 data/users.json and data/tasks.json

Create the data files deliberately

  • Use one file for users and one for tasks so the comparison with the SQL model stays clear.
  • Start with a sensible initial structure rather than leaving the files mysterious.
Step 2 app.py

Write the JSON load and save helpers before the routes

  • Keep the repeated file logic in helper functions rather than duplicating it inside every route.
  • Explain what each helper returns and when it should be called.
Step 3 Project map

Keep frontend parity in view

  • Notice that the browser-facing HTML and JavaScript can stay very similar.
  • The major difference is now the backend storage logic.

What should be secure before the live JSON features

  • The class understands which parts of the app stay the same across both tracks.
  • The role of `data/*.json` is clear before feature implementation starts.
  • The JSON track is positioned as a storage-model variation, not as a completely different app.
